Belongeth
be-LONG-eth
v. (3rd sing.)
Archaic third-person singular of belong, formed with the -eth ending standard in the Authorized Version. Webster 1828 defines BELONG as to be the property of; to be the concern or proper business of; to be appendant to. In the KJV the word settles questions of ownership — of land, of office, and above all of vengeance and of power.

Biblical Definition

Belongeth answers the question whose is it? and in the KJV that question is usually settled against us. To me belongeth vengeance, and recompence (Deuteronomy 32:35) — the verse Paul and Hebrews both quote to take the sword out of the believer’s hand. God hath spoken once; twice have I heard this; that power belongeth unto God (Psalm 62:11) — not chiefly, not derivatively, but as His own. The word also assigns duty and place. This is it that belongeth unto the Levites: from twenty and five years old and upward they shall go in to wait upon the service of the tabernacle (Numbers 8:24) — the office has an owner and an age. Towns belong to tribes: Gibeah belongeth to Benjamin (Judges 19:14), Shochoh belongeth to Judah (1 Samuel 17:1), Zarephath belongeth to Zidon (1 Kings 17:9), where God sends His prophet to be fed by a Gentile widow. And the New Testament applies it to maturity: strong meat belongeth to them that are of full age, even those who by reason of use have their senses exercised to discern both good and evil (Hebrews 5:14). Every use draws a line of ownership, and the lines are God’s to draw.

Webster 1828 Definition

Webster 1828 defines BELONG as to be the property of; to be the concern or proper business of; to be appendant or related to. BELONGETH is the archaic third-person singular retained throughout the Authorized Version.

expand to see more

BELONG, v.i. — To be the property of; as, the house belongs to the man.

To be the concern or proper business of; to appertain; as, it belongs to the magistrate to judge.

To be appendant to; to be connected with; to have relation to.

Webster’s three senses map the biblical uses: property (Psalm 62:11), proper business or office (Numbers 8:24; Hebrews 5:14), and appurtenance of place (Judges 19:14).

Key Scripture

Numbers 8:24 — "This is it that belongeth unto the Levites: from twenty and five years old and upward they shall go in to wait upon the service of the tabernacle of the congregation:"

Deuteronomy 32:35 — "To me belongeth vengeance, and recompence; their foot shall slide in due time: for the day of their calamity is at hand, and the things that shall come upon them make haste."

Psalm 62:11 — "God hath spoken once; twice have I heard this; that power belongeth unto God."

1 Kings 17:9 — "Arise, get thee to Zarephath, which belongeth to Zidon, and dwell there: behold, I have commanded a widow woman there to sustain thee."

Hebrews 5:14 — "But strong meat belongeth to them that are of full age, even those who by reason of use have their senses exercised to discern both good and evil."

Modern Corruption

The corruption is theft of what belongs to God — vengeance taken into private hands, and power treated as a human possession to be seized, negotiated, or distributed rather than received.

expand to see more

Deuteronomy 32:35 is quoted twice in the New Testament for one purpose: to stop a Christian avenging himself. Dearly beloved, avenge not yourselves, but rather give place unto wrath: for it is written, Vengeance is mine; I will repay, saith the Lord (Romans 12:19), and again at Hebrews 10:30. The prohibition is not a counsel of niceness; it is a property claim. Vengeance belongs to God, and the believer who takes it has stolen. Scripture does not thereby abolish justice — the magistrate beareth not the sword in vain (Romans 13:4), and the state is God’s appointed avenger — but it removes the sword from the offended man’s own hand. The distinction between personal retaliation and civil justice is exactly the distinction the modern age blurs in both directions.

Psalm 62:11 answers the age’s theory of power. If power belongs to God, then every human authority holds it on loan and answers for its use, and no framework that treats power as the fundamental social reality — something groups possess, seize, or are denied — can be adopted as an explanation of the world. Scripture’s categories for injustice are sin, the fallen heart, covenant-breaking, and the oppression of the poor, the widow, the orphan, and the stranger, all of which name real wrongs and name them before God. The believer’s comfort in the psalm is that the same verse which humbles the powerful assures the weak: the power in question is not finally in the hands of the men who are using it against them.

Greek & Hebrew Roots

The Hebrew has no single verb to belong; possession is expressed with the preposition le, to or for. Deuteronomy 32:35 is literally to me vengeance, and the KJV supplies the verb.

expand to see more

English -eth — the third-person singular ending standard in 1611 and retained throughout the Authorized Version.

Hebrew le (the lamed preposition) — to, for, belonging to; Deuteronomy 32:35 reads to me vengeance and recompence.

Hebrew naqam (H5359) — vengeance; the noun God claims as His own in Deuteronomy 32:35.

Hebrew 'oz (H5797) — strength, power; power belongeth unto God (Psalm 62:11).

Greek esti with the genitive in Hebrews 5:14 — is of the full-grown; the KJV renders the genitive of possession with belongeth.

Usage

"To me belongeth vengeance, and recompence (Deuteronomy 32:35) — quoted at Romans 12:19 and Hebrews 10:30 to disarm the believer."

"Power belongeth unto God (Psalm 62:11) — heard twice because said once; the ground of both humility and comfort."

"Strong meat belongeth to them that are of full age (Hebrews 5:14) — maturity earns its diet by use, not by age alone."
